outcome: Admission to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)
cohort: The study included singleton term pregnancies (>=37 weeks) with a documented positive Group B Streptococcus vaginal-rectal culture obtained within 5 weeks before delivery.
finding: Among GBS-positive term patients, intrapartum clindamycin prophylaxis was associated with significantly higher maternal infectious morbidity (intrapartum fever, clinical chorioamnionitis, postpartum fever, postpartum antibiotic use) and increased GBS detection in chorioamniotic cultures compared with ampicillin, with no significant differences in neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery rates did not differ significantly between patients receiving clindamycin versus ampicillin.
